record.paper_title: Open problems in stochastic reinforcement models
record.context_brief: Local limits beyond affine preferential attachment
record.original_question: For preferential attachment models with general attachment functions f beyond the affine case, and with a fixed number m > 1 of out-edges per arriving vertex, identify and prove the local weak limits. In particular, extend beyond the known tree case m=1 despite the absence, for graph models with m>1, of both the continuous-time branching-process embedding used for trees and the Polya urn representations available in the affine case.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 24 (Local limits preferential attachment models beyond the affine case)
The local limits for such models, but now with a fixed number of out-edges per vertex, has not been considered beyond the tree case for which m = 1

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a dynamic random graph model constructed as follows. Fix an integer m ≥ 2 and a function f: ℤ_{≥0} → (0,∞) (the attachment function). Starting from a finite initial graph G_{n_0}, at each time step n+1 a new vertex v_{n+1} arrives and creates exactly m out-edges, each independently attaching to an existing vertex u of the current graph G_n with probability proportional to f(deg_{G_n}(u)) (with conditional independence or appropriate sequential sampling of the m endpoints from the same vertex distribution). When f(k) = k + δ (δ > -m), this is the affine (Barabási–Albert-type) preferential attachment graph; the case m = 1 yields the preferential attachment tree.

For a finite graph G with a distinguished root vertex, let (G, o) denote the rooted graph viewed up to rooted isomorphism. Equip the space 𝒢_* of rooted locally finite graphs with the local (Benjamini–Schramm) topology. Let o_n be a uniformly random vertex of G_n.

Problem: For general attachment functions f beyond the affine case and for m > 1, identify the local weak limit (G_n, o_n) ⇒ (G_∞, o_∞) in 𝒢_*, i.e., exhibit an explicit rooted random graph (G_∞, o_∞) such that for every finite rooted graph (H, o') and every r ≥ 0,

   ℙ(B_r(G_n, o_n) ≅ (H, o')) → ℙ(B_r(G_∞, o_∞) ≅ (H, o'))   as n → ∞,

where B_r denotes the r-neighborhood of the root. Prove the convergence. The challenge is that the continuous-time branching-process embedding available when m = 1 and the Pólya urn representation available in the affine case both fail in this regime, so new techniques are required.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work has made substantial progress. Hazra, van der Hofstad, and collaborators ("Universality of the local limit of preferential attachment models", arXiv:2212.05551) identify local limits (a random Pólya point tree) for a broad class of preferential attachment models with m ≥ 1, and subsequent work on "Local weak limits for collapsed branching processes with random out-degrees" further extends to general attachment functions via a continuous-time branching process construction with collapsing. The problem of fully general attachment functions f beyond affine with arbitrary fixed m > 1 thus appears partially solved, with universal local-limit results established under suitable conditions on f.

status_evidence.title: Universality of the local limit of preferential attachment models
status_evidence.snippet: Substantially extends previous work by Berger et al. by identifying the local limit of preferential attachment models where vertices enter with i.i.d. random numbers of edges; limit is the random Pólya point tree.
status_evidence.claim: Local limits identified for preferential attachment models beyond the simple affine case, including with multiple out-edges per vertex.

status_evidence.title: Local weak limits for collapsed branching processes with random out-degrees
status_evidence.snippet: Evolving directed random graph obtained by collapsing a continuous-time branching process; incoming nodes arrive in families with random sizes and connect with probability proportional to a general attachment function f of the node's degree.
status_evidence.claim: Local weak limit established via collapsed branching processes for general attachment functions and random/multiple out-degrees.
